cards.title: Today’s vocabulary
sections: thanks a lot · /ˌθæŋks ə ˈlɑt/ · fixed expression · Phrase · New
a friendly way to thank someone warmly. Thanks a lot for your help.
thank you very much · /ˌθæŋk ju ˌvɛri ˈmʌtʃ/ · fixed expression · Phrase · New
a polite way to express strong thanks. Thank you very much for the book.
no problem · /ˌnoʊ ˈprɑbləm/ · fixed expression · Phrase · New
a casual reply showing that helping was not difficult. Thanks for waiting. No problem.
my pleasure · /maɪ ˈplɛʒɚ/ · fixed expression · Phrase · New
a polite reply showing that you were happy to help. Thank you for the lesson. My pleasure.
friendly and willing to help others. It is kind of you to help me.

cards.title: Say thanks
sections: Tongue tip lightly at or between the teeth. Join the sounds into one word without adding extra vowels.
Listen. Say it. Record a second attempt after checking one sound.
cards.name: Everyday English - A1 - Day 009 - Pronunciation & Listening - 01

articulation.label: thanks
articulation.alt: thanks: /θ/ → /æ/ → /ŋ/ → /k/ → /s/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /θ/: Tongue tip lightly at or between the teeth.
/æ/: Low front tongue; open the jaw.
/ŋ/: Back of tongue at soft palate; air through nose.
/k/: Back of tongue meets the soft palate; release.
/s/: Make a narrow gap near the ridge; let air flow.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.
